propositions: Whole-tree build-provenance fixtures export 3,019 checkout files but production hatch_build.py consumes only three (hook, pyproject.toml, src/rebar/__init__.py), causing redundant session initialization across xdist workers and 56–67% slower per-worker setup times.

The artifact-probe workflow builds with GITHUB_SHA instead of deriving the final checked-out HEAD and asserts truthiness rather than exact SHA equality, accepting wrong but nonempty provenance on Gerrit patchsets.

A shared minimal committed Hatch package fixture with production hook and real isolated PEP 517 boundary preserves all semantics (env override, git fallback, blank-env failure, sdist preservation, shallow-source) while reducing serial elapsed from 18.23s to 9.11s (50% improvement) and per-worker setup from 6.60–6.74s to 2.20–2.88s (56–67% improvement).

The artifact-probe workflow must derive REBAR_EXPECTED_COMMIT using git rev-parse --short HEAD after the lane-specific final checkout and enforce exact SHA equality for both wheel and installed sdist distributions.
